content:
**Key observations from the image:**

- Tomato leaves (identifiable by leaf shape and serration)
- Multiple dark brown to nearly black lesions on the upper leaf surface
- Lesions are roughly circular to irregular, with **visible concentric rings** (target-spot / bullseye pattern)
- Lesions are moderate in size (several mm to ~1 cm+, confirmed by the US quarter for scale)
- No white fuzzy sporulation on undersides (rules out Late Blight)
- No tan/gray small spots (rules out Septoria)
- No salmon-colored spore masses or water-soaked sunken appearance (rules out Anthracnose)
- No overall bronzing or mosaic pattern (rules out viral diseases)

**Reasoning:**

The concentric ring "bullseye" pattern on dark brown lesions is the hallmark of Early Blight (*Alternaria solani*). The symptom description confirms: "lesions are larger and darker brown than Septoria leaf spots and display concentric rings." The lesion size and darkness further distinguish this from Septoria Leaf Blotch (which produces smaller, tan-to-gray spots without concentric rings). Late Blight lesions would appear water-soaked with pale green halos and white fuzzy growth underneath. Everything points to Early Blight.
